description: Tang Yuan are soft, chewy glutinous rice balls traditionally eaten during Chinese festivals like Winter Solstice and Chinese New Year. They symbolize family reunion and completeness, often served in a sweet ginger soup or with various fillings. This delightful dessert offers a comforting and subtly sweet experience, perfect for sharing with loved ones.

ingredients.notes: also known as sweet rice flour

instructions.title: Prepare the Black Sesame Filling
instructions.text: In a food processor, grind the toasted black sesame seeds with 30g granulated sugar until fine. Add the softened lard or unsalted butter and process until a thick paste forms. Roll the paste into small balls, about 1/2 inch in diameter, and chill them in the refrigerator for 15 minutes to firm up.

instructions.title: Make the Glutinous Rice Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, gradually add warm water to the glutinous rice flour while mixing with your hands. Continue kneading until a smooth, pliable dough forms that is not sticky. The dough should be soft but firm enough to hold its shape. Adjust water or flour as needed.

instructions.title: Form the Tang Yuan Balls
instructions.text: Take a small portion of dough, about 1 inch in diameter, and flatten it into a disc. Place a chilled black sesame filling ball in the center. Carefully wrap the dough around the filling, pinching the edges to seal, then roll gently between your palms to form a smooth sphere. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling. For plain Tang Yuan, simply roll the dough into small balls without filling.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ginger Soup
instructions.text: In a medium pot, combine 1 liter of water, sliced ginger, and rock sugar. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes, allowing the ginger flavor to infuse and the sugar to dissolve completely. Taste and adjust sweetness if desired.

instructions.title: Cook the Tang Yuan
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Carefully drop the Tang Yuan balls into the boiling water, stirring gently to prevent them from sticking. Cook until the Tang Yuan float to the surface, then continue cooking for another 1-2 minutes to ensure they are thoroughly cooked through and soft.

instructions.title: Serve the Tang Yuan
instructions.text: Using a slotted spoon, transfer the cooked Tang Yuan directly into bowls of the warm ginger soup. Serve immediately while hot. Garnish with a few extra slices of ginger from the soup if desired.

tips: Achieve the perfect dough consistency by adding water gradually. The dough should feel like soft play-doh – not too sticky, not too crumbly. If it's too dry, add a tiny bit more water; if too wet, add a sprinkle of glutinous rice flour.
Experiment with different fillings! Popular alternatives include crushed peanuts with sugar, red bean paste, or even a simple brown sugar syrup pocket for a burst of sweetness.

Tang Yuan are best enjoyed fresh. If you have leftovers, store them in the ginger soup in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop or microwave until warm, adding a splash of water if the soup has thickened.
